english.title: Record image under clothing to observe another without consent
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), recorded an image beneath the clothing of another person of the genitals or buttocks, or underwear covering the genitals or buttocks, of that person, in circumstances where the genitals, buttocks or underwear would not otherwise be visible, with the intention that you or a third person would look at the image for the purposes of

(A)_[obtaining sexual gratification,]_
(B)_[humiliating, alarming or distressing that person,]_

doing so without consent and without reasonably believing that the person consented
english.legislation: Contrary to section 67A(2) and (4) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) It makes no difference whether the victim of the offence is exposed or covered with underwear for the purpose of this offence.
(ii) As per section 67A(3)(a), if the offence is being committed for sexual gratification, the gratification can be for the person recording the offence or for other persons.
(iii) As per section 68(1A), for the purpose of the section, operating equipment includes enabling or securing activation by another person without their knowledge.
(iv) Victims of this offence are entitled to anonymity under section 2 of the Sexual Offences (Amendment) Act 1992.

other.penalty:
Either way -Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 67A(4)(a) and (5) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
